preread.instruction: Read this entire preread block before beginning any research step. Every open question listed here is still open. Every constraint listed here is still active. Findings from prior passes that conflict with these definitions must be flagged, not silently resolved in the game's favor.

game_identity.name: Match-3 Farkle Frenzy
game_identity.core_fusion: Spatial match-3 drag-chain mechanics (select adjacent tiles on a grid by dragging) FUSED WITH Farkle dice scoring (the face values of selected tiles ARE the dice rolled). These are not adjacent systems. One drag-chain action simultaneously clears board tiles AND evaluates a Farkle combination. This is the central design claim.

question.text: Should singleplayer Farkle events carry any partial recovery mechanic?
question.current_state: Hard negative. Board shakes. Unbanked resets to zero. Multiplier resets to x1.0. No redemption path. Banked points are untouched.
question.what_is_needed: A recommendation grounded in research — not a summary of what other games do. Does hard failure produce more memorable sessions than softened failure? Compare Balatro (full run ends), Yahtzee (single turn lost, game continues), Candy Crush (lives gate). The answer is NOT decided. Research must decide it.

question.text: There is no decision timer on Continue/Bank/Pass.
question.current_state: The active player can deliberate indefinitely. The 3-second reaction window applies only to non-active players voting. Energy meter drains passively in Frenzy mode but that is not a decision timer — it is a resource cost.
question.constraint: Do not recommend adding a decision timer without explicit evidence that untimed decisions produce worse engagement than timed ones in comparable push-your-luck games. The default assumption is untimed. Burden of proof is on recommending a timer, not on keeping the current state.

question.current_state: When a player Passes in Rally mode, the incoming player inherits board state, full unbanked total, and current multiplier step. No decline mechanic exists. The 3-second reaction window allows voluntary signaling (hold thumbs-down = "pass to me") but does not allow refusal of an incoming pass.
question.constraint: This is intentional design. Do not recommend a refusal mechanic without explicit evidence it would improve team dynamics in comparable cooperative games.

question.text: All role synergies are emergent — no hardcoded cross-role interactions exist.
question.current_state: Conductor passing to Rainmaker at x3.0 so Rainmaker receives x4.0 is the strongest synergy in the game. It is entirely emergent from the Pass mechanic and timing. There is no coded bonus for using both roles together. This is not a bug. It is the current design.
question.constraint: The research must rule on whether hardcoded synergies should be ADDED. Do not describe emergent synergies as if they are hardcoded. The prior pass made this error.

question.text: Suspected role imbalance at high skill levels.
question.developer_hypothesis: Conductor: near-mandatory (compounding benefit on every Pass is too efficient to skip at high skill). Archivist: undervalued (value collapses when skilled teams rarely Farkle, keeping the pool small). Headhunter: situational (power scales with Stone blocker density, which is a lobby configuration setting). Rainmaker: highest ceiling, lowest floor (Straight chains are rare, so ability fires infrequently).
question.constraint: Confirm or refute each hypothesis with named evidence from benchmark games. Do not validate hypotheses by restating them. Do not refute them without counter-evidence.

If research reveals a claimed novelty is not novel, state this directly with the counter-evidence and the name of the game that constitutes prior art. False confirmation of novelty wastes more development resources than accurate negation does. This instruction overrides any diplomatic impulse to hedge or partially confirm a refuted claim.

carry_forward_findings.finding: Pandemic: On the Brink Archivist has hand limit 8 and can retrieve discarded city cards. This is a candidate partial prior art for Novelty Claim 3. One element (designated recovery role) is present. Whether the shared-loss-buffer element is also present requires verification in step 4.
Overwatch Lucio and Brigitte function as Conductor benchmarks via "skill-to-value curve" — value only realized through positional mastery, not raw output.

Balatro: additive modifiers (+Mult) process before multiplicative modifiers (xMult). This processing order is what makes high-value Joker builds feel exponential. Applicable to Farkle's multiplier ladder feel.

Bust rates cited (66.7% at 1 die, 44.4% at 2 dice, 15.7% at 4 dice) are from independent dice probability model — NOT from the 60-tile pool model. These figures are incorrect for Farkle Frenzy and must be recalculated in step 6.

Slay the Spire: skilled winners embrace 1.82x more randomness (Entropic options) than losers. High-level play is adaptive agency, not randomness elimination. Supports keeping spawn pool variance high rather than tightening it.

Hades: Mirror of Night converts failed run currency into permanent upgrades. Failure becomes anticipation, not frustration. Primary template for any singleplayer redemption mechanic if OQ1 recommends one.

gaps.gap: Novelty claims 1-4 were never researched. Steps 2-5 of the follow-up plan produced zero output. No verdicts exist.
Per-role scorecard was not produced. Prior pass gave qualitative descriptions only. No Legibility / Strategic Depth / Synergy Potential / Uniqueness ratings exist for any of the four roles.
Bust probability data uses standard independent dice model, not the 60-tile pool model. The figures are wrong for this game. No corrected table exists.
EV inflection point calculation was not completed. The hardest Continue/Bank decision points have not been identified.
Open question OQ1 (singleplayer Farkle redemption) was never engaged. Prior passes treated it as settled. A recommendation is required.

step.title: Role Scorecard
step.instruction: Apply the Pandemic, Overwatch, Puzzle and Dragons, and Rocket League benchmarks already completed in passes 1 and 2 to produce scored entries for all four Farkle roles. Where benchmark evidence is insufficient, conduct targeted additional research as specified below.

research.question: Does the Pandemic On the Brink Archivist role become less valuable at high skill levels when teams play aggressively and rarely discard cards they need?
research.apply_to: Farkle Archivist, whose 15%-per-chain pool recovery becomes near-worthless when a skilled team rarely Farkles and the Farkle Pool stays near zero.
research.hypothesis_to_test: Archivist undervalued at high skill. Confirm or refute with Pandemic evidence.

research.question: Do Lucio or Brigitte in Overwatch create near-mandatory pick patterns at high competitive ranks? If yes, what design interventions were used or proposed?
research.apply_to: Farkle Conductor, which adds one multiplier step on every Pass — a compounding benefit that applies on every turn transition and may be too efficient to skip at high skill.
research.hypothesis_to_test: Conductor near-mandatory. Confirm or refute with Overwatch evidence.

research.question: In cooperative games with high-ceiling/low-floor roles, does infrequent ability activation kill engagement or amplify it? (The Rainmaker's ability fires only on Straight chains — the rarest 6-tile combination in the scoring table.)
research.find: Games where a role's defining ability fires rarely but produces outsized payoff when it does. How do players sustain engagement during the stretches where their role is inactive?

research.question: In cooperative games, do roles whose value scales with external session configuration feel specialized or broken?
research.context: Headhunter destroys Stone Blockers in one hit instead of two. Stone Blocker density is a lobby setting (LOW / MEDIUM / HIGH). On LOW density, Headhunter has almost nothing to do. On HIGH density, it is the most impactful role on the board. The player cannot change this after the session begins.
research.find: Cases where a role's power was configuration-dependent and how those games communicated this dependency to players at selection time.

step.synergy_ruling: Produce a ruling: should hardcoded cross-role synergies be added, or is emergent synergy sufficient? Ground the ruling in benchmark findings. Do not describe current emergent synergies as if they are hardcoded — this error occurred in pass 2 and must not recur. Reference OQ4 before writing this section.

step.title: Novelty Claim 1 — Skill-Expressed RTP
step.claim: Skilled players can provably push RTP above 100% through the game's intended design mechanics — not through exploits, not through card-counting equivalents, not through temporary promotions. The 102% ceiling is built into the base game design.
step.search_scope: Non-blockchain consumer browser or mobile casino games. Release date: 2010 to present. Exclusions: professional gambling training tools, strategy simulators, games where 100%+ RTP is achieved only through a bonus/promotion, games where the mechanic is an unintended exploit.
step.prior_art_threshold: A game constitutes prior art ONLY if ALL of the following are true: (a) It is a casino game with real or virtual monetary stakes. (b) Expert play, using the game's intended mechanics, can push expected RTP above 100% over a sufficient sample size. (c) This property is part of the base game design, not a loophole. (d) The game is consumer-facing (not a professional tool).

step.title: Novelty Claim 2 — Spatial Dice
step.claim: The tiles a player chains ARE the dice they roll. Spatial position determines which values are evaluated. No separate dice-rolling step exists. Board position determines both the dice rolled AND the resulting board state after commit.
step.search_scope: All gaming platforms. All release dates.
step.prior_art_threshold:
A game constitutes prior art ONLY if ALL of the following are true: (a) Players select or chain tiles spatially on a grid or board. (b) The face values of those tiles are evaluated against a defined Farkle-style combination table (Three of a Kind, Straight, etc.) — NOT against a simple match-by-color or match-by-type rule. (c) Both (a) and (b) occur in the SAME committed action with no intermediate dice-rolling step between selection and scoring.
NOT prior art: - Match-3 games with color matching only (no face-value evaluation). - Games with match-3 mechanics AND a separate adjacent dice minigame. - Games where dice values are assigned randomly to tiles after selection.
step.partial_confirmed_instruction: If PARTIALLY_CONFIRMED: specify which element is present (spatial selection OR combination scoring) and which is absent.

step.title: Novelty Claim 3 — Farkle Pool and Recovery Role
step.claim: Points lost to Farkle events flow into a shared loss-buffer (the Farkle Pool). A dedicated role (Archivist) has the explicit primary ability of recovering 15% of that pool per scoring chain. Both elements must be present and structurally linked.
step.candidate_prior_art: Pandemic: On the Brink Archivist role has a hand limit of 8 and can retrieve discarded city cards. Confirmed: designated recovery role exists. UNVERIFIED: whether a shared loss-buffer that accumulates specifically from failure events is also present. This must be resolved in this step.
step.mandatory_sources: Spirit Island | Arkham Horror: The Card Game | Gloomhaven | Aeon's End | Pandemic: On the Brink (resolve CPA1)
step.prior_art_threshold:
Prior art requires ALL of the following simultaneously: (a) A shared resource buffer that accumulates from failure events (not a general shared resource pool that exists at all times). (b) A dedicated player role whose PRIMARY defined ability specifically drains or recovers from that buffer (not a role that can optionally interact with it as a secondary effect). (c) Both (a) and (b) are structurally linked — the buffer only has value because of the role, and the role's primary identity is defined by the buffer.
Element (a) alone is not prior art. Element (b) alone is not prior art. Both elements present but not linked is PARTIALLY_CONFIRMED.
step.partial_confirmed_instruction: Name the game. Specify which element is present. Specify which element is absent or structurally unlinked.

step.title: Novelty Claim 4 — Inherited Full Liability
step.claim: When a player Passes in Rally mode, the incoming player inherits the ENTIRE team-accumulated unbanked total — not just the current player's contribution. If the incoming player Farkles, they lose points that multiple players built across multiple turns. The spatial board context, the inherited multiplier step, and the reaction window vote are part of the mechanic.
step.mandatory_sources: Traditional Farkle rules (official and variants) | Cosmic Wimpout | Can't Stop | Zombie Dice | Yahtzee (tournament variants) | Pickomino / Heckmeck
step.prior_art_threshold:
Prior art requires ALL of the following: (a) A turn-handoff mechanic where one player passes to another. (b) The incoming player inherits the FULL accumulated unbanked total from ALL previous players in the current streak — not just the passing player's single-turn contribution. (c) If the incoming player fails (Farkles), the entire inherited total is lost — including contributions from players who are no longer active in the current streak.
NOT prior art: - Games where only the current roller's score is at risk on pass. - Games where the incoming player can choose to start fresh. - Cooperative games where accumulated resources persist but cannot be lost to a Farkle-equivalent event. - Traditional Farkle's "keep rolling" option (only current turn score is at risk, not prior players' contributions).
step.partial_confirmed_instruction: Specify the exact degree of overlap. Name which element of the claim has prior art and which does not.

step.title: Corrected Probability Math — 60-Tile Pool Model
step.correction_target: The bust rates cited in pass 2 are from the standard independent dice model (each die rolled independently with P=1/6 per face). Farkle Frenzy uses a pre-shuffled pool of exactly 60 tiles: 10 of each face value (1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6). Tiles are drawn without replacement per pool cycle. This is a fundamentally different probability system — draws are correlated, not independent. The cited figures are wrong for this game. Do not use them.

pool_model.distribution: 10 of each face value (1 through 6), equal
pool_model.assumption: Calculate from full pool state (60 tiles, 10 of each) — this represents the equal-distribution baseline and produces the most stable probability estimates for design purposes.

deliverable_1.name: BustProbabilityTable
deliverable_1.instruction: Calculate P(score = 0 | chain length = N) for N = 1 through 6. Score = 0 means the drawn face values, evaluated against the complete Farkle scoring table below, produce no scoring combination.

scoring_table.combo: Three of any other face = face*100 pts
Four of a kind plus pair (6 tiles) = 1500 pts
scoring_table.rule: Combinations stack (max-partition). A chain scores the maximum achievable by any non-overlapping partition.

deliverable_1.thresholds_to_identify: P(Farkle) crosses 10% at chain length: [N] P(Farkle) crosses 25% at chain length: [N] P(Farkle) crosses 50% at chain length: [N]

deliverable_2.name: EVInflectionTable
deliverable_2.instruction: Calculate the expected value of CONTINUE vs BANK at each combination of chain length (1-6) and multiplier step (x1.0 through x4.0). Use the corrected bust probabilities from deliverable_1. Assume average scoring chain = 350 pts (representative midpoint for planning purposes — not a hard figure, adjust if research surfaces a better estimate). Identify combinations where EV(CONTINUE) and EV(BANK) are within 10% of each other — these are the genuinely hard decisions and the design target for the ladder's most impactful steps.

deliverable.title: Per-Role Scorecard
deliverable.content: Complete 4x4 scorecard using the schema declared in step 1. Synergy ruling (hardcoded vs emergent) with evidence. Improvement recommendations per role. All improvement recommendations labeled LOW / MEDIUM / MAJOR_REWORK.

deliverable.title: Novelty Claim Verdicts
deliverable.content: Four verdicts in schema format. Cross-reference all findings from passes 1, 2, and 3 before finalizing each verdict. Do not soften refutations — reference OQ6.

verdict.detail: [for PARTIALLY_CONFIRMED: element present and element absent]

deliverable.title: Corrected Probability Tables
deliverable.content: BustProbabilityTable (chain lengths 1-6, pool model). EVInflectionTable (chain length x multiplier, hard decisions flagged). Replace all figures from pass 2 with corrected figures. Do not include the old incorrect figures anywhere in the output.

deliverable.title: OQ1 Recommendation — Singleplayer Farkle Redemption
deliverable.content: A recommendation: should singleplayer Farkle events carry a partial recovery mechanic? The answer must be YES or NO with supporting evidence. A summary of what other games do is not sufficient — a recommendation is required. Use CF5 (Slay the Spire adaptive agency finding), CF6 (Hades Mirror of Night model), and the push-your-luck calibration research from pass 1 as primary inputs. If YES: specify what form the mechanic should take and label it LOW / MEDIUM / MAJOR_REWORK. If NO: specify what visual or mechanical changes to the existing hard failure state would maximize its emotional impact without adding a redemption path.
deliverable.constraint: Do not recommend a redemption mechanic simply because other games have one. Confirm it would improve Farkle Frenzy specifically.

output_rules.rule: Every finding names the specific Farkle mechanic it applies to. No orphaned observations.
Every recommendation labeled: LOW / MEDIUM / MAJOR_REWORK. No unlabeled recommendations in any section.
When a researched mechanic is similar but not identical to a Farkle mechanic, report both the similarity and the exact differences. Do not collapse similar into "already exists."
Failures in comparable designs are as valuable as successes. If a mechanic similar to Farkle's was tried and abandoned or criticised, report this directly.
Do not re-summarize findings from passes 1 or 2. Produce only what was missing. The gap declaration above defines exactly what was missing.
Prior art thresholds are declared per step. Do not expand or contract them. A game that meets 2 of 3 threshold criteria is PARTIALLY_CONFIRMED, not CONFIRMED and not REFUTED.
Begin response with: FRENZY ANALYST — PASS 3 ENGAGED. GAPS LOADED. PRE-BRIEF READ.
